about: Section 13 words of AC-2a and AC-2b-D. <name> marks a value filled in at run time; "\n" in cli and mail is a line break. nav is 12.4's left navigation in order, the reserved places carrying phase 4 and 5 (not rendered in AC-2a). cef maps an audit action to its CEF name (AC-2a 13.1, AC-2b-D 13.6); actions not in it use the action. metrics_help holds the # HELP words of every 10.1 family. key-record.* are the app loopback page's words quoted in 3.9. script is AC-2b-D 13.6, the install scripts' words.

page.meet-ca.title: Meeting Hub organization CA
page.meet-ca.none: This console holds no organization CA.
page.meet-ca.warn: This console will hold your organization's Meeting Hub CA in its sealed storage. Anyone who breaks into this console could then make certificates for any person in your organization and act as them on every Meeting Hub relay that trusts this CA. Any High relay that trusts this CA loses its High protection; such relays cannot join this console.
page.meet-ca.high: Under the High profile the organization CA stays on its own signer. This console does not hold it.
page.meet-ca.create-next: Create a new CA (coming next, with device certificates issued here)
page.meet-ca.import-help: Upload ca.crt and ca.key from your CA folder, and issued.json and crl.pem so revocations are kept. From now on, only this console signs this CA's revocation lists: stop signing them on the PC and on a certificate server in root mode.
page.meet-ca.signer-help: If a certificate server signs your people's devices, enter its address (https://...). Relays then fetch its revocation list; without it they refuse those devices.
page.meet-ca.remove: Remove the CA from this console
page.meet-ca.remove-elsewhere: I will sign this CA's revocation lists elsewhere before <date>.
page.meet-ca.diverged: <relay> holds a revocation list of this CA that another signer made. Its revocations were added here. Stop the other signer.
page.meet-ca.lost: The CA key cannot be opened (sealing lost). Import it again before <date>, when relays that trust it stop accepting anyone.
page.meet-ca.unreadable: The CA records do not read back. Nothing is issued until they do.
page.spokes-root.title: Remote Spokes organization root
page.spokes-root.help: The root's public key, root.pub. Relays this console installs check it against your license before they trust it. Never upload the private key.
page.attention.meet-ca-expiring: The Meeting Hub organization CA ends in <days> days.
page.attention.meet-ca-lost: The Meeting Hub organization CA key cannot be opened. Relays that trust it stop accepting anyone after <date>.
page.attention.meet-ca-unreadable: The Meeting Hub organization CA records do not read back.
page.attention.meet-crl-failing: The Meeting Hub organization CA's revocation list could not be renewed. It ends <date>.
page.attention.meet-crl-diverged: Another signer is making revocation lists for the Meeting Hub organization CA (seen on <relay>).
page.attention.meet-crl-future: A revocation list for the Meeting Hub organization CA is dated in the future (<date>, seen on <where>). Its revocations were added here; fix that signer's clock.
page.relay.fleet-ca-held: The Admin Console at <origin> holds the CA this High relay trusts, so it takes no changes from that console. Move this relay to a CA the console does not hold.
page.meet-ca.confirm-no-high: No High Meeting Hub relay anywhere, in this console or not, trusts this CA.
page.meet-ca.crl-number-ceiling: That revocation list's number is too high to follow, so this console did not sign a newer one. Decide which signer stays.
page.deploy.remove-signer-note: This relay can still reach the certificate server at <url> until its certificate there ends (<date>), because that server is not marked as checking revocation. Remove the host's address from the server's allowed relays now.
page.attention.profile-lock-refused: <relay> refused to start on <date> because its configuration said <configured> while the host is locked to the High profile.
page.meet-ca.crl-not-pushed: <relay> trusts this CA but does not take revocation lists from this console (<why>).
page.meet-ca.crl-fixed: its crl setting names a fixed file
page.meet-ca.crl-none: it checks no revocation list yet; turning one on would change who it accepts
page.attention.relay-meet-cert-expiring: The TLS certificate of <relay> ends in <days> days and has not renewed.
page.attention.relay-signer-cert-expiring: The certificate <relay> uses with the certificate server ends in <days> days and has not renewed. When it ends, people whose devices come from that server stop being accepted on <relay> within 7 days.
page.attention.signer-crl-mismatch: <relay> says the certificate server at <url> does not check revocation, so relays using that server get 30-day certificates until it agrees or you turn the setting off.
page.attention.meet-crl-size: The organization CA's revocation list is <size> KB, half of what relays accept. Remove entries that no longer matter on the CA page.
page.meet-ca.signer-enforced: This certificate server checks revocation of relay certificates
page.meet-ca.signer-enforced-help: Turn on only after the server runs a version that checks revoked relay certificates. Relays using it then get 90-day certificates, as long as every one of them confirms.
page.meet-ca.prune-help: Upload the certificate itself. It is removed only if this CA signed it and it has already ended. Entries older than <days> days leave the list on their own.
page.meet-ca.max-lifetime: Longest lifetime of any certificate this CA has issued (days)
page.attention.signer-crl-stale: The certificate server at <url> still holds revocation list <number>, older than this console's. Relays it refuses are not refused there yet.
page.deploy.docker-turn-note: On Docker this installer writes no host firewall, so calls between two people who both need TURN do not work until you open UDP 49160 to 49260 toward this host's own address in your firewall.

enroll.title: Make an enrollment code for <name>?
enroll.body: Anyone with the code can join one <product> relay to this console in the next hour.

confirm-relay.title: Confirm <name>?
confirm-relay.body: Fingerprint <fingerprint>. Confirm only if the relay printed the same.

label.title: Rename <name>?
label.body: Only this console's name for it changes.

narrow-scopes.title: Remove <scopes> from <name>?
narrow-scopes.body: This console can no longer use them on the relay.

widen-scopes.title: Ask <name> for <scopes>?
widen-scopes.body: The relay's operator must accept before they apply.

remove-relay.title: Remove <name> from the console?
remove-relay.body: The relay keeps running and keeps its people. This console loses access to it.

endorse.title: Confirm <n> new keys for <m> relays?
endorse.body: These people can then make changes on those relays.

invite-meet.title: Ask for <email> to be invited to Meeting Hub on <relay>?
invite-meet.body: An admin of that relay completes the invite in the Hub app.

import.title: Send <n> invites?
import.body: <c> console invites and <m> Meeting Hub requests on <r> relays.

suspend.title: Suspend <name> on <relay>?
suspend.body: Their <n> devices are blocked on this relay for <hours> hours. Other relays are not affected.

unsuspend.title: Lift the suspension of <name> on <relay>?
unsuspend.body: Their devices work on this relay again.

remove-person.title: Remove <name> from <relay>?
remove-person.body: Revocation requests go to the relay's admins for each of <n> devices.

token.title: Create a scrape token for <label>?
token.body: It reads health metrics of <relays> for <days> days.

siem-on.title: Send events to <host>:<port>?
siem-on.body: A test message goes first; the change applies only if it arrives.

siem-off.title: Stop sending events to the SIEM?
siem-off.body: Audit and security events stop leaving this console.

local-read-only-on.title: Set this relay read only from the console?
local-read-only-on.body: The Admin Console can still read; it can change nothing here.

local-read-only-off.title: Let the console make changes again?
local-read-only-off.body: Changes still need an admin's confirmation, checked here.

local-confirm.title: Run this change from the console?

local-accept-scopes.title: Give the console <scopes>?
local-accept-scopes.body: It can then use them on this relay.

endorse-key.title: Endorse your Admin Console key for <relay host>?
endorse-key.body: Only your recorded key <label> is endorsed. The relay then trusts it for the console at <origin>.

local-trust-ca.title: Trust the new management CA?
local-trust-ca.body: Fingerprint <fingerprint>. Only if a console admin read you the same one by phone or in person.

server-revoke.title: Replace the management certificate now?
server-revoke.body: Relays drop the old one as soon as they get the new trust list. Use this if the console's key may have been copied.

ca-rollover.title: Start management CA <generation>?
ca-rollover.body: Every relay's operator must confirm its fingerprint on the relay within 90 days, or that relay stops connecting.

roster-cancel.title: Cancel <hint> on <relay>?
roster-cancel.body: The console may fail to deliver this. Also call the relay's operator to refuse the key on the relay.

local-leave.title: Leave the Admin Console at <origin>?
local-leave.body: This relay stops sending health and stops taking changes from it. Its own console stays.

meet-ca-import.title: Import the CA <id> into this console?
meet-ca-import.body: This console then holds the key that vouches for every person in your organization, and only it signs this CA's revocation lists. Any High relay that trusts this CA would lose its High protection.

meet-ca-revoke.title: Revoke certificate <serial>?
meet-ca-revoke.body: Relays refuse it once they get the new revocation list.

meet-ca-remove.title: Remove the CA from this console?
meet-ca-remove.body: The sealed key is wiped. The last revocation list is valid until <date>; after that, relays that trust this CA refuse everyone unless another signer renews it.

spokes-root.title: Use root <id> for new Remote Spokes relays?
spokes-root.body: Relays this console installs trust it only when it matches their license.

setup-needed.words: Finish the first step of setup first.

setup-code.words: That setup code is not right. It is in setup-code.txt on the console's host.

fleet-product.words: This code is for a <product> relay. Run it on a <product> relay.

fleet-pin.words: This console's identity does not match the code. Ask the console's admin for a new code.

fleet-preview-changed.words: The console changed since you checked it. Run the command again.

fleet-profile.words: This console and this relay are not in the same security profile. A High relay works only with a High console, and a High console only with High relays in FIPS mode.

enroll-limit.words: Too many open enrollment codes. Use or cancel one first.

fingerprint.words: That fingerprint does not match this relay. Do not confirm it.

fleet-scope.words: This relay did not give the Admin Console the <scope> scope.

fleet-scope-unknown.words: This relay does not know the scope <scope> yet.

fleet-route.words: This page is not available through the Admin Console.

fleet-stepup.words: The relay could not verify your confirmation. Try again.

meet-ca-high.words: Under the High profile the organization CA stays on its own signer. This console does not hold it.

meet-ca-high-relay.words: A High Meeting Hub relay trusts this CA, may trust it (it has not reported which CAs it trusts), or is still joining, so this console cannot hold it.

meet-ca-confirm.words: Confirm that no High Meeting Hub relay anywhere trusts this CA.

meet-ca-seal.words: Holding the organization CA needs a sealing provider bound to this host (systemd credential or Windows service account). Run lucid-relay console seal-setup --role console.

meet-ca-exists.words: This console already holds an organization CA. Remove it first.

meet-ca-key.words: That key does not belong to that CA certificate, or it is not a P-256 CA valid for 120 more days.

meet-ca-signer.words: Enter the certificate server as https:// and its host name.

meet-ca-in-use.words: <n> relays still use certificates from this CA. Confirm that you will sign its revocation lists elsewhere.

meet-ca-lost.words: The CA key cannot be opened. Import it again.

meet-ca-prune.words: That certificate was not issued by this CA, is not on the list, or has not ended yet. A revocation stays while its certificate can still be used.

spokes-root-key.words: That is not a P-256 public key. Upload root.pub, never the private key.

spokes-root-license.words: No license in the library names root <id>.

cli.cli.enroll-preview:
Console: <origin>
This relay: <name> (<site>), <product>
Scopes: <scopes>
Profile: <profile>, two-person control <on or off>
Admin keys the console offers (none is trusted until its admin endorses it or you list its fingerprint):
<one line per entry: email, role, key hint, verified as a security key or not>
cli.cli.enroll-ask: Join this console? Type yes to continue:
cli.cli.enroll-next: Saved. Start the relay within the hour; it joins the console at start and prints its fingerprint.
cli.cli.enrolled: Joined the Lucid Admin Console at <origin> as <relayId>. Fingerprint: <fingerprint>. An admin there confirms it.
cli.cli.enroll-high-standard: This relay is in the High profile and that console is Standard. A High relay joins only a High console.
cli.cli.fleet-running: Stop the relay first, or use its Admin Console.
cli.cli.fleet-state-needed: Joining a console needs the relay's state folder (--state).
cli.cli.not-enrolled: This relay is not managed by a Lucid Admin Console.
cli.cli.left: This relay left the Lucid Admin Console at <origin>.
cli.cli.with-console-both: A relay that runs the console role does not also run its own console: drop --console or console_port.
cli.cli.with-console-host: The console's public host name must differ from the relay's host names.
cli.cli.setup-code-file: Setup code for the Lucid Admin Console. Enter it on the first page. It changes at every start until setup is done.
cli.cli.console-needs-public: the console needs --public <host name> (passkeys need a DNS name)
cli.cli.enroll-ask-code: Enrollment code (it is not shown as you type or paste):
cli.cli.code-file: The code file must be a regular file only you can read.
cli.cli.bootstrap-wait: This relay trusts no admin key yet. Each admin endorses their key from the IDE plugin or the Hub app (Endorse my Admin Console key), or you add their key fingerprints with --fleet-admin-key when enrolling.
cli.cli.bootstrap-done: This relay now trusts <n> admin keys (<m> wait 24 hours under High).
cli.cli.with-console-high: Under the High profile the console and the relay must run as two services with separate accounts. Drop --with-console or with_console.
cli.cli.state-acl: Under the High profile the state folder <path> must be open only to this service's account and administrators. Run lucid-relay console seal-setup.
cli.cli.console-identity: The console must not run as the relay's account. Run lucid-relay console seal-setup --role console.
cli.cli.trust-ca: New management CA fingerprint: <fingerprint>. Confirm only if a console admin read you the same one by phone or in person.
cli.cli.trust-time-reset:
Trusted time: <T>
Stored trust list: number <storedSeq>, issued <storedIssuedAt>
Newer trust list from the console: number <seq>, issued <issuedAt>
This host's clock: <wall>
Use the newer trust list and set trusted time to <issuedAt>? Type yes to continue:
cli.cli.recover: This relay's management key is lost. Ask a console admin for a Replace code for <name>, then run lucid-relay enroll again.
cli.cli.connect-dns: The console's host name did not resolve.
cli.cli.connect-tcp: The console's management port did not answer.
cli.cli.connect-tls-protocol: The console and this relay share no allowed TLS settings.
cli.cli.connect-server-untrusted: The server is not the console this relay trusts (its certificate, name or trust list did not match).
cli.cli.connect-certificate-refused: The console refused this relay's certificate. It may have been removed from the console, or its certificate ended.
cli.cli.connect-upgrade-refused: The console answered but did not open the channel.
cli.cli.connect-closed: The connection closed before the channel opened.
cli.cli.deploy-preview:
Relay DNS name: <host>
TURN: <turnHost>
Relay admins: <admins>
Profile on this host: <profile>
Certificate: <certificate source>
Organization root: <id> (<root source>)
License: <license line>
cli.cli.deploy-source-console-ca: from the organization CA held by this console
cli.cli.deploy-license-none: none: the relay starts stopped until a license is installed
cli.cli.deploy-ask-admins: Relay admins: their email addresses, separated by commas:
cli.cli.deploy-admins-needed: Without a terminal, give the relay admins with --admins.
cli.cli.deploy-ask-fingerprints: Admin key fingerprints, one per line, as each admin read them from Your account, Key fingerprints for relays (an empty line ends; none is fine):
cli.cli.deploy-offered-key:
The console offers the key of <email> (<hint>), who made this code, as this relay's first admin key. This console's installer put this relay's program here for this code, so trusting its key adds nothing it could not already do.
Fingerprint: <fingerprint>
Type yes to trust it (anything else skips it):
cli.cli.deploy-not-offered: The console offered an admin key, but this relay does not take it (no installer mark from this console for this code, it is High, it already has state, or that admin is not in this relay's admins). Use fingerprints or endorse from the IDE plugin or the Hub app.
cli.cli.deploy-ask-turn-host: TURN name or address (Enter for the DNS name):
cli.cli.deploy-ask-clients: Networks that may reach this relay (addresses with a prefix, separated by commas):
cli.cli.deploy-host-differs: The console's code says <field> is <console value>, but this host says <host value>. Nothing was saved.
cli.cli.deploy-root-id: Organization root: <id>. Check it against your own records.
cli.cli.deploy-root-differs: The console names root <id>, but the root placed on this host is <placed id>. Nothing was saved.
cli.cli.deploy-anchor: This relay does not take an organization root from the console (High, or its program did not come from the console). Place it with --root or --pki-dir. Nothing was saved.
cli.cli.deploy-profile: This relay is Standard and that console is High. A High console takes only High relays.
cli.cli.deploy-profile-changed: This host was installed with the <profile> profile. Uninstall with --purge to change it.
cli.cli.deploy-pki: The code says the certificate comes from <source>, but this host was set up for <other>.
cli.cli.deploy-high-preview: This High relay was offered a certificate, root or admin key by the console. A High relay takes none of these from the console. Nothing was saved.
cli.cli.deploy-next: Saved. The installer now starts the relay; it joins the console and prints its fingerprint.
cli.cli.deploy-fingerprint:
Relay fingerprint: <fingerprint>
In the Admin Console, check that it shows the same fingerprint, then press Confirm relay.
cli.cli.deploy-not-deploy: This code was made for a relay that is already installed. Run the command without --deploy.
cli.cli.deploy-needs-deploy: This code was made for a new install. Run the install command from the Admin Console, or ask for a code for an already installed relay.
cli.cli.deploy-env: This code was made for <env>, not <this env>.
cli.cli.deploy-pki-high: Under the High profile a relay does not take its certificate from the Admin Console. Set fleet_pki to false and place the certificate files.
cli.cli.deploy-no-cert: This relay has no certificate yet. Run the install command again with a new code, or place its certificate files.
cli.cli.deploy-no-root: This relay has no organization root yet. Run the install command again with --root <file>.
cli.cli.deploy-marker-other: This installer was fetched for a different code (<marker enrollment>), so it does not count as installed by the console for this one. Run the command shown with this code.
cli.cli.profile-locked: This host is locked to the High profile (<lock path>), but the relay's configuration says <configured>. Set the profile to high; the relay does not start otherwise.

script.script.usage: Usage: install (the default) or uninstall [--purge]. Options: --profile high or standard, --admins <emails>, --host <name>, --turn-host <name>, --clients <CIDRs>, --pki-dir <folder>, --ca <file>, --root <file>, --code-file <path>, --external-ip <public>[/<private>], --allow-peer <CIDR>, --ssh-from <CIDR>, --no-firewall, --firewall-force, --binary <path>, --console <url>, --pins <pins>.
script.script.os: This installer supports Debian 12 or 13 and Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04. This host is <os>.
script.script.arch: This console hands out the relay program for <arch>; this host is <host arch>.
script.script.no-tty: No terminal to read the enrollment code from. Run the command in an interactive shell, or pass --code-file <path> (owned by root, mode 600) and --admins.
script.script.disk: At least 2 GB must be free under /opt and /var/lib.
script.script.port-busy: Port <port> is already in use by <process>. Free it and run the command again.
script.script.hand-installed: This host already runs a relay that was installed by hand. Use Already installed in the Admin Console to join it.
script.script.ask-government: Is this a government deployment? A yes uses the High security profile, which cannot be changed later. (yes or no) [yes]:
script.script.ca-file: The CA file must be a self-signed P-256 CA certificate (ca.crt), never its key.
script.script.profile-header: This console serves Standard relays only. Install a High relay from your release media.
script.script.checksum: The downloaded relay program does not match SHA-256 <sha256>. Nothing was installed.
script.script.binary-digest: Relay program SHA-256: <sha256>. It must match your release notes.
script.script.runs: The relay program does not run on this host: <why>
script.script.high-binary: Pass --binary <path> with the verified lucid-relay from your release media.
script.script.pki-dir: The folder must hold ca.crt, relay.crt and a matching relay.key, and relay.crt must come from ca.crt.
script.script.root-file: The root file must be a P-256 public key (root.pub), never the private key.
script.script.root-needed: Pass --root <file> with your organization root's public key.
script.script.firewall-exists: This host already has a firewall (<kind>). Open these ports in it: <ports>.
script.script.firewall-other: Other services listen on this host: <list>. The firewall would close them. Run again with --firewall-force to close them, or --no-firewall and open <ports> yourself.
script.script.firewall-applied: Firewall: SSH (<ports>) from <from>; relay ports <ports>; everything else closed. Local connections to this host's own public or LAN addresses follow the same rules; use 127.0.0.1 for other local services.
script.script.firewall-no-ssh: No SSH service found; the firewall allows no SSH.
script.script.firewall-changed: The firewall on this host changed while installing, so no firewall table was written. Resolve it and run the command again; if the enrollment code was already used, make a new one in the Admin Console.
script.script.turn-self: This installer did not write a firewall here, so TURN may not relay to this host's own addresses. Calls between two people who both need TURN fail until you open UDP 49160 to 49260 toward <addresses> in your firewall and run again with --allow-peer for those addresses.
script.script.busy: Another run of this installer is in progress. Wait for it to finish.
script.script.docker-needed: Install Docker Engine and its Compose plugin first.
script.script.docker-high: Docker is not offered under the High profile.
script.script.waiting: Starting the relay and joining the console...
script.script.join-timeout: The relay did not join within 2 minutes. Last log lines:
script.script.updated: This relay already belongs to this Admin Console. Updated the program to <version> and restarted it.
script.script.other-console: This relay belongs to another Admin Console (<url>). Nothing was changed.
script.script.downgrade: This host runs version <installed>, newer than <version>. Nothing was changed.
script.script.done-meet: Done. Relay https://<host> on TCP 443; TURN <turnHost> on UDP and TCP 3478, TCP 5349 and UDP 49160 to 49260.
script.script.done-spokes: Done. Relay https://<host>:8443. Add this entry to your hubs' relay directory:
script.script.left: The relay left the Admin Console.
script.script.left-offline: The console was not reached; the relay removed its link here. Remove it in the Admin Console too.
script.script.uninstall-done: Removed the relay program and its services. Kept <folders>; add --purge to delete them.

mail.fleet-invite-waiting.subject: A Meeting Hub invite is waiting for you
mail.fleet-invite-waiting.body:
<requester> asked for <email> to be invited to Meeting Hub on <relay>.
Open the Hub app as an admin of that relay to complete or decline it.
It ends in 14 days.

fleet.mail.license-reminder.subject: The <product> license of <relay> ends in <days> days
fleet.mail.license-reminder.body:
The <product> license of <relay> ends on <date>.
Install a new license before then from the License page of the Admin Console.
If it ends, <relay> stops serving people after at most 2 days of grace.

fleet.mail.license-grace.subject: <relay> stops on <date and time> unless a new license is installed
fleet.mail.license-grace.body:
The <product> license of <relay> has ended.
Service stops on <date and time> unless a new license is installed.
Install one from the License page of the Admin Console.

fleet.mail.license-stopped.subject: <relay> stopped: no active license
fleet.mail.license-stopped.body:
<relay> stopped serving people because it has no active <product> license.
The Admin Console can still reach it. Install a license from the License page and it starts again.

cef.fleet.relay.label: Rename <name>
cef.people.invite: Ask for <email> to be invited to Meeting Hub on <relay>
cef.fleet.bootstrap-anchor: Endorse your Admin Console key for <relay host>
cef.fleet.meet-ca.import: Import the Meeting Hub organization CA <id>
cef.fleet.meet-ca.remove: Remove the Meeting Hub organization CA
cef.fleet.spokes-root.set: Set the Remote Spokes organization root <id>
cef.fleet.meet-ca.prune: Remove certificate <serial> from the revocation list
cef.fleet.meet-ca.signer-enforced: Mark the certificate server <url> as <checking or not checking> revocation

metrics_help.lucid_console_info: Version, security profile and FIPS mode of this Lucid Admin Console.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_up: 1 when the relay is connected and sent health in the last 3 minutes.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_last_contact_seconds: Seconds since the relay was last in touch.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_health: The relay's health as the console judges it; 1 for the current state.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_devices_online: Meeting Hub devices online on the relay.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_calls_active: Meeting Hub calls with two or more people.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_call_minutes_total: Meeting Hub call minutes since the console started.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_messages_total: Messages relayed since the console started.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_hubs_online: Hubs that checked in during the last 5 minutes.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_spokes_online: Spokes that checked in during the last 5 minutes.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_spokes_total: Spokes seen in the last 30 days.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_spokes_busy_total: Spokes that sent or received mail, summed per minute since the console started.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_lanes_busy: Busy lanes on the relay's spokes.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_lanes_total: Live lanes on the relay's spokes.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_cpu_process_percent: CPU used by the relay process, percent of the host.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_cpu_host_percent: CPU busy on the relay's host, percent.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_mem_process_bytes: Memory held by the relay process.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_mem_host_used_percent: Memory in use on the relay's host, percent.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_network_receive_bytes_total: Bytes received by the relay's host since the console started.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_network_transmit_bytes_total: Bytes sent by the relay's host since the console started.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_conn_open: Open connections on the relay's listeners.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_latency_console_seconds: Round trip from the relay to the console.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_cert_tls_days: Days left on the relay's TLS certificate.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_cert_console_days: Days left on the relay's own console certificate.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_cert_mgmt_days: Days left on the relay's management certificate.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_cert_signer_days: Days left on the Meeting Hub signer certificate.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_crl_days: Days until the relay's revocation list needs its next update.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_license_days: Days left on the relay's license; negative in grace.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_quota_hits_total: Requests refused for quota since the console started.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_license_state: The relay's license state; 1 for the current state.
metrics_help.lucid_relay_license_service: Whether the relay serves people under its license (on, grace, upgrade-period or stopped); 1 for the current state.
